In `docs/runbooks/ci-gate.md`, in the existing \"Early PR preflight\" section, add a short \"Measured results (2026-09-25)\" subsection.

- Baseline before phase A (459 CI runs, 2026-09-22 20:24Z to 2026-09-24 23:07Z): 89% of PR runs take the full tier; time to first

84: ## Repo-wide tests always run in the selected and docs tiers (#8707)
85: 
86: Import selection can never pick a test that scans the repository's own trees:
87: the Changes job links a changed `scripts/foo.py` to `tests/**/test_foo*.py` (and
88: a changed `tests/test_x.py` to itself), but a test scanning `tests/` or
89: `scripts/` has no import edge to the changed module. That is how PR #8692
90: merged green on the selected tier and then turned `main` red on shard 3 for
91: every full-tier run: `tests/test_lint_test_assertions.py::test_repo_test_suite_is_clean`
92: scans all of `tests/` and was never selected for a `tests/orchestration/test_thread_handoff.py`
93: change.
94: 
95: Such tests carry the `repo_wide` marker (registered in `pyproject.toml`). After
96: the candidate run, a `selected` shard runs the marked set under its own narrow
97: allowlist:
98: 
99: ```
100: git ls-files -- tests | grep -E '/test_[^/]+\.py$' \
101:   | xargs -r grep -lE 'pytest\.mark\.repo_wide' | sort
102: LU_PYTEST_SHARD_FILES=<that list> pytest tests \
103:   -m 'repo_wide and not slow and not atlas_release' -n logical --dist=loadfile ...
104: ```
105: 
106: The narrow allowlist keeps collection cheap (the full tree is ~2 minutes to
107: collect); the known set currently runs ~400 tests in under two minutes. An
108: empty list fails the step loudly. The grep matches the exact marker
109: declaration, not a bare `repo_wide` mention, so a comment or an unrelated
110: string cannot pull a file into the allowlist (the `-m` filter would skip it
111: anyway, but the list stays honest).
112: 
113: The **docs lane** runs the same `-m repo_wide` invocation after its
114: `docs_skills` run. Docs-lane PRs reach no other pytest leg, and several
115: repo-wide scanners read `docs/`: `tests/test_work_privacy.py`,
116: `tests/test_agent_fleet_tooling_guardrails.py`, and
117: `tests/test_public_tree_no_baked_host_run_root.py`. A docs-only PR that adds a
118: baked host path under `docs/` is therefore caught before merge.
119: 
120: The **content lane** deliberately runs no `-m repo_wide` leg: content mode runs
121: `-m 'reads_content and not slow and not atlas_release'` (plus the shard safety
122: net), so a scanner of a content root is selected by its `reads_content` marker
123: without a repo-wide pass. Which lane a content-only PR reaches decides whether
124: that marker is enough:
125: 
126: - A PR whose paths are all content-class and include a `site/src/content/docs/`
127:   path lands on the **content lane**, which runs `reads_content`: scanners of
128:   that tree, for example `tests/test_site_links.py`, run here.
129: - A PR touching only `curriculum/` or `wiki/` — no `site/src/content/docs/`
130:   path — is docs-only and lands on the **docs lane**. Since #8720 the docs lane
131:   also runs `-m 'reads_content and not slow and not atlas_release'` (under the
132:   same narrow allowlist as the `repo_wide` leg) whenever the flag
133:   `docs_reads_content` is `true`, which `classify_changes.py` sets only for a
134:   docs-lane result with some path under `curriculum/` or `wiki/`. This closes
135:   the gap that let PR #8712 (a docs-only change) merge green and turn `main`
136:   red on the next full-tier run: `docs/epics/fresh-build-build-program.md` is a
137:   hashed source of every `curriculum/l2-uk-en/lesson-plans/<lvl>/_decisions.yaml`,
138:   and `tests/curriculum/arc/test_decisions_record.py` (a `reads_content` module)
139:   went red on `main`. A few curriculum and wiki scanners are marked `repo_wide`
140:   and ran there before #8720: `tests/test_ohoiko_source_inventory_scope.py`,
141:   `tests/test_prompt_template_render.py`, `tests/test_a1_review_scores.py`,
142:   `tests/test_aggregate_findings.py`, `tests/test_schema_validation.py`
143:   (`test_a2_plans_match_module_schema`), and the reference checks in
144:   `tests/test_skill_instruction_routes.py`; the new `reads_content` leg is what
145:   covers the rest.
146: 
147: Repo-wide tests that read a content tree and must also run on the content lane
148: carry `reads_content` as well: `tests/test_llm_reviewer_dispatch.py`,
149: `tests/test_threshold_source_of_truth.py`, `tests/test_sparse_collection_guard.py`,
150: `tests/test_public_tree_no_baked_host_run_root.py`,
151: `tests/api/test_app_factory.py`, and
152: `tests/test_curriculum_upgrade_no_host_run_root.py` are marked both ways, and
153: none is `slow`/`atlas_release`.
154: 
155: `tests/test_repo_wide_marker_invariant.py` keeps the marker honest. Marker
156: detection is syntactic and per-function (AST): a test counts only when its own
157: `@pytest.mark.repo_wide` decorator, its class decorator, or a module-level
158: `pytestmark` contains `pytest.mark.repo_wide`, so decorator order and comments
159: do not matter and a module with two scanners and one marker fails. The
160: authoritative guarantee is the explicit registry of known repo-wide
161: modules/functions plus a reasoned `NOT_REPO_WIDE` escape hatch; the AST
162: heuristic over each test module (repo-rooted `.glob`/`.rglob`,
163: `os.walk`/`os.scandir`, `git ls-files`/`ls-tree` through `subprocess`, and
164: known whole-tree linters, propagated through helper calls) is a best-effort
165: net. The invariant also fails when the selected tier or the docs lane drops
166: its `-m repo_wide` invocation.
167: 
168: No CF attest. No auto-arm. No landing-class classifier. No coverage floor.
169: Red team review is out of band.
170: 
171: ## Early PR preflight (#8750 phase A)
172: 
173: The `Preflight` job reports a broken repo-wide invariant (a missing
174: `subprocess` timeout, the test-assertion lint, the marker invariants) in a few
175: minutes instead of after a full pytest shard. Before it, the p50 time to the
176: first failed job on a full PR run was about 13 minutes.
177: 
178: **When it runs.** `scripts/ci/classify_changes.py` decides once and emits
179: `preflight`. `preflight_for()` returns `true` only for a `pull_request` event
180: whose tier is `full` or `selected`: the tiers whose shards run the
181: `repo_wide` set. The Preflight job's `if:` and CI Gate both read that one
182: output, and nothing in `ci.yml` re-derives it. The other lanes get no
183: preflight:
184: 
185: - The **docs** lane already runs `repo_wide` in its single short shard.
186: - The **content** and **frontend** lanes do not run `repo_wide` at all, so a
187:   preflight there would change what the gate proves.
188: - **`merge_group`, `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch`** always get
189:   `preflight=false`.
190: 
191: A `full-ci` label or a classifier failure on a PR forces `full`, and so turns
192: preflight on.
193: 
194: **What it runs.** It uses the same allowlist construction and flags as the
195: shards' `repo_wide` leg. An empty allowlist fails the step loudly:
196: 
197: ```
198: LU_PYTEST_SHARD_FILES=<repo_wide list> pytest tests \
199:   -m 'repo_wide and not slow and not atlas_release' --strict-markers \
200:   -n logical --dist=loadfile --max-worker-restart=0 --timeout=120 \
201:   --timeout-method=thread --override-ini addopts=-v
202: ```
203: 
204: A second invocation then runs the files registered in the job's
205: `PREFLIGHT_EXTRA_TESTS` env, one path per line, under
206: `-m 'not slow and not atlas_release'` with the same flags. These are cheap
207: invariants that fail often but are not `repo_wide`. Today the list holds only
208: `tests/curriculum/arc/test_decisions_record.py`, the cross-file hash
209: invariant that caused 7 of the 40 sampled PR failures. On its own it takes
210: about 5 s. An empty list also fails loudly. `tests/test_ci_preflight.py`
211: checks that every registered path exists and is not already `repo_wide`.
212: Both invocations always run, so one run reports every broken invariant; the
213: step fails if either one failed.
214: 
215: **Setup.** Preflight uses the same Python and uv install as the shards, and
216: the same Atlas manifest hydrate. It leaves out the Postgres service, Node/npm
217: and the native apt packages (bubblewrap, libpq, apparmor), because no
218: `repo_wide` test uses them: no marked file mentions a Postgres DSN,
219: `psycopg` or `bwrap`, and the one that mentions `npm` stubs it. The checkout
220: is shallow. The whole selection passes in a fresh depth-1 clone with no
221: Postgres DSN and no `node_modules`. `timeout-minutes: 8`.
222: 
223: **Parallel, not gating.** No shard `needs: preflight`, and the shards still
224: run the `repo_wide` tests as the backstop, so a green run is no slower.
225: Nothing is cancelled when preflight fails. Preflight only makes the red
226: signal arrive earlier.
227: 
228: **CI Gate rule.** This rule lives in the gate step:
229: 
230: - `preflight=true`: the Preflight result must be `success`. `failure`,
231:   `cancelled` and `skipped` all fail the gate.
232: - `preflight=false`: the Preflight result must be `skipped`.
233: - If Changes itself did not succeed, the gate fails before it reaches this
234:   rule.
235: 
236: `merge_group` and nightly runs have no preflight. Their gate evaluation is
237: unchanged apart from the `preflight=false → skipped` branch.
238: 
239: **Superseded runs.** A new push to the same PR cancels the superseded run
240: through the workflow `concurrency` group. CI Gate is `if: always()`, so it
241: still runs for that stale SHA and fails there (see the `concurrency` comment
242: in `ci.yml`). That red lands on a commit that is no longer the PR head. The
243: replacement run on the new head is the one that decides the PR.
244: 
245: ## pytest shard collection and balance (ci-shard-balance-2026-09-07)
246: 
247: The code pytest shards run on all 4 runner vCPUs (`-n logical`, not `-n auto`
248: which counts physical cores), collect through one initial `tests` path
249: instead of positional file arguments, and balance by measured per-file
250: duration instead of a modulo split. Full-tier shard count (`4`) is declared
251: once in `ci.yml`'s workflow-level `env: PYTEST_SHARD_COUNT`. The Changes job
252: emits `shard_count` (1 or 4) and `shards`; `plan-files` always uses
253: `needs.changes.outputs.shard_count` so selected mode never LPT-partitions a
254: candidate set into unused buckets.
255: `--max-worker-restart=0` fails the job on a worker crash: pytest-timeout's
256: thread method terminates the process, and replacing it can leave xdist
257: hanging until the job limit.
258: 
259: Dispatch workers are a separate host from these runners. SCOPE for #8645
260: part B: this guards workers against accidental xdist fan-out and concurrent
261: full suites. It is not a sandbox against deliberate evasion; parts A (memory
262: admission) and C (per-worker cgroup) are the hard limits.
263: 
264: When `LEARN_UKRAINIAN_DISPATCH_TASK_ID` is set, `scripts/ci/pytest_dispatch_cap.py`
265: clamps xdist to two workers. `pyproject.toml` `addopts` still passes
266: `-p ci.pytest_dispatch_cap`, and `scripts/delegate.py` also sets
267: `PYTEST_PLUGINS=ci.pytest_dispatch_cap` (appended when the variable is already
268: set). `build_agent_env` forwards that variable into the agent CLI only while
269: the dispatch marker is set, and only as the single entry
270: `ci.pytest_dispatch_cap` — any other comma-separated plugin name is dropped.
271: A worker that copies CI's `--override-ini addopts=-v` therefore still loads
272: the cap. The `pythonpath` ini key is separate from `addopts` and still
273: makes `ci.pytest_dispatch_cap` importable. The plugin is idempotent when both
274: registrations load it. `-n auto`, `-n logical`, and an explicit `-n` use
275: `--maxprocesses=2`. A `--tx` spec whose expanded worker count is greater than
276: 2 (for example `--tx 3*popen`) is a usage error before configuration; the cap
277: does not rewrite the spec. A full-suite invocation takes one non-blocking lock
278: under `/var/tmp/lu/learn-ukrainian/` (`LU_PYTEST_FULL_SUITE_LOCK` overrides
279: that path). The fd is stored on the pytest config that acquired it and
280: released only in that run's `pytest_unconfigure`, so a nested `pytest.main()`
281: does not drop the outer run's lock. CI does not set the dispatch variable
282: (see `.github/workflows/`), so shard `-n logical` is unchanged. A second
283: full-suite run on a dispatch host fails immediately and tells the worker to
284: run targeted tests.
285: 
286: **Collection — allowlist hook.** `tests/conftest.py` implements
287: `pytest_ignore_collect`, gated on env var `LU_PYTEST_SHARD_FILES`: unset,
288: collection is completely unchanged (local dev, `docs_skills` lane); set, it
289: must point at a readable, non-empty, newline-delimited list of repo-relative
290: `test_*.py` paths with no duplicates — anything else (missing, unreadable,
291: malformed, empty) raises loudly at first collection. Directories are never
292: filtered by the hook: it explicitly admits them and allowed files, overriding
293: pytest's default `norecursedirs` exclusions such as `build`; other files are
294: ignored. This preserves the tracked-file selection, including `tests/build/`.
295: 
296: **Balance — `scripts/ci/pytest_shards.py` file plane.** Two new subcommands,
297: extending the existing planner (Cursor Cloud's node-ID plane — `plan` /
298: `plan-shard` / `run` / `verify-artifacts` — is untouched):
299: 
300: - `plan-files --shard-id N --shard-count K --durations <json> --output <path>`:
301:   reads candidate repo-relative file paths from stdin (`ci.yml` pipes in
302:   `git ls-files -- tests | grep -E '/test_[^/]+\.py$' | sort`), LPT-assigns
303:   them across `K` shards from the committed duration snapshot (median
304:   fallback for files without history), writes shard `N`'s sorted allowlist,
305:   and prints every shard's predicted weight.
306: - `file-durations --junit <xml>... --output <json>`: refreshes the committed
307:   snapshot from JUnit reports. Aggregation policy: a JUnit
308:   `<testcase time="...">` already sums setup+call+teardown for that node
309:   (pytest's own writer combines the three), so no phase decomposition is
310:   attempted; the same node ID appearing in more than one report (a rerun, or
311:   the same file spanning several reports) keeps the maximum, not the sum,
312:   before per-file totals are formed; a testcase whose `classname`/`name`
313:   doesn't resolve to a repo test file is skipped and counted, never raised.
314: 
315: **Snapshot refresh procedure.** After a landing-tier CI run (`merge_group` or
316: `push` to `main`), download each shard's uploaded `pytest-junit-shard-N`
317: artifact and run:
318: 
319: ```
320: .venv/bin/python scripts/ci/pytest_shards.py file-durations \
321:   --junit pytest-shard-1.xml --junit pytest-shard-2.xml \
322:   --junit pytest-shard-3.xml --junit pytest-shard-4.xml \
323:   --output scripts/ci/pytest-file-durations.json
324: ```
325: 
326: Commit the refreshed snapshot (sorted keys, 3-decimal rounding) when shard
327: balance measurably drifts — not on every green run.
328: 
329: ## Cloud advisory runner dependency parity (#6977 slice A)
330: 
331: `scripts/ci/cursor_cloud_full_pytest.sh` (the offline-verifiable Cursor cloud
332: pytest prototype; see `docs/design/2026-09-06-cloud-agent-pytest-advisory.md`)
333: mirrors this job's "Install Python deps" and "Hydrate Atlas lexicon manifest"
334: steps: same lockfile exclude set (`torch`/`torchvision`/`open_clip_torch`/
335: `stanza`), `uv pip` when available, `packages/v4-runtime --no-build-isolation`
336: + `build_assets.py`, and an unconditional hard-fail manifest hydrate. It also
